background.definition: Fatigue is a feeling of weariness, tiredness, or lack of energy. CFS is diagnosed when the following is present for at least 3 of 6 months and is moderate to severe in intensity: (a) a substantial reduction in the ability to engage in pre-illness levels of activity accompanied by fatigue not substantially alleviated by rest, (b) post-exertional malaise and (c) unrefreshing sleep. A recent Institute of Medicine report advocated for renaming CFS to to a more descriptive name, "systemic exertion intolerance disease" (SEID). Their rationale was that (a) CFS trivializes the syndrome, and (b) myalgic encephalitis should be rejected as a name as their is no evidence of brain inflammation.

list.listitem: An estimated 3 million visits were made to physicians' offices in 2005 with a resulting principal diagnosis of general fatigue.
An estimated 177,000 visits were made to hospital outpatient departments in 2005 with a resulting principal diagnosis of general fatigue.
Fatigue is more common in women than men.
There are between 830,000 and 2.5 million Americans with CFS according to the Institute of Medicine.

The prevalence of clinically significant fatigue has varied between 44% and 85% in surveys of populations with HIV, COPD, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, lupus, and primary biliary sclerosis.
Estimated annual cost to employers exceeds $136 billion in lost productive work time.
Depression and anxiety are the most common causes of fatigue (40%-60%).

Fatigue commonly remains unexplained a year later. A Dutch study enrolled 571 patients with a chief complaint of fatigue. A year later, only 47% had a final diagnosis (19.4% musculoskeletal, 16.5% psychological or social, 8.1% digestive, 6.7% neurologic, and 4.9% respiratory).
See section below for differential diagnosis.
Pathophysiology will vary depending on the underlying cause.
In patients with cardiac, pulmonary, and metabolic abnormalities, fatigue may be due to altered oxygen and nutrient delivery.
If patient has a connective tissue disease or an infectious disease, fatigue may be due to factors released as part of the inflammatory response.

The loosely categorized autonomic dysfunction syndromes include chronic fatigue, complex regional pain syndrome, and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Administration of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is not associated with an increase risk of developing any of these syndromes.
Among the patients with longstanding fatigue, only one third meet the CDC criteria for chronic fatigue syndrome. C
Graded aerobic exercise has been shown to result in improvements in fatigue and physical functioning in patients with fatigue.A

Differential.Differential_Features: Loss of energy, sleep problems, poor appetite, depressed mood
Cold intolerance, constipation, weight gain, dry skin
Dyspnea, headache, palpitations, pallor, progressive weakness
Febrile, tonsillar exudate, adenopathy, abnormal LFTs, skin rash
Reproducible pain, chronic headache, reduced physical endurance
Abdominal pain, mucus in stool, constipation alternating with diarrhea
Sweating, weight loss, muscle fatigue, physical weakness
Dyspnea on exertion, crackles at the lung bases, S3 gallop, tachycardia
Weight loss, night sweats, fever, atypical lymphadenopathy
Onset of fatigue coincidental with COVID-19 infection

list.listitem: The first step in the evaluation of the patient with unexplained fatigue in the primary care setting is a careful history. The focus should be on signs of depression, duration of symptoms, symptom severity, and the degree to which they interfere with work and social functioning. Specific causes and their signs and symptoms are discussed below and in the Differential Diagnosis section.

The cause of fatigue in many patients will be unexplained even after thorough evaluation and the cause will often remain unexplained 1 year later.
Depression: screen all patients presenting with fatigue for depression with a validated instrument such as the PHQ depression score. Hypothyroidism: hair loss, cold intolerance, slowed reflexes, dryness of skin, mental lethargy. Anemia: conjunctival pallor, history of bleeding (eg, menorrhagia or dark stools), palpitations, dyspnea; symptoms are typically progressive. Infection: fever, weight loss. For long COVID onset coincidental with COVID-19 infection. Malignancy: weight loss, pain, night sweats, fever, atypical lymphadenopathy. Collagen vascular disease: rash, joint pain, myalgias, reduced physical endurance.
Because of the high incidence of psychological causes and the broad differential diagnosis of physical cause, laboratory tests have a low yield in the work-up of patients presenting with fatigue.

The initial evaluation should include a CBC, sedimentation rate, TSH, and glucose. Additional testing should be ordered only to follow up on specific findings in the history, physical examination, or initial laboratory evaluation.
If infection is suspected, begin with purified protein derivative, HIV testing, hepatitis panel, and Lyme titer.
Hepatitis panel: jaundice, risk factors for hepatitis B or C.
Order a CXR for patients with dyspnea, cough, and abnormal lung sounds.
Order an ECG for patients with chest pain, dyspnea, or other cardiovascular symptoms. An echocardiogram is recommended for patients with heart murmur or signs of heart failure.
See chapters on anemia, hypothyroidism, depression, Lyme disease, and tuberculosis for more on their diagnostic evaluations.
Refer to the algorithm in for a suggested approach to the patient with fatigue.
Stimulants and exercise may be helpful in cancer-related fatigue.

In a Cochrane review of exercise in patients with CFS, exercise therapy (including aerobic activity such as walking, swimming, cycling or dancing with intensities ranings from low to vigorous) was associated with a reduction in fatigue symptoms and improved sleep when compared to passive controls, but not when compared to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
A single large dose of vitamin D 100,000 units increased blood vitamin D levels but did not affect fatigue to a clinically greater extent than placebo.

A meta-analysis of seven trials with 1033 participants (in community-dwelliong aadults over the age of 60 with) demonstrated modest improvement (SMD -0.40) in fatigue with the following interventions: mindfulness meditation, muscle relaxation, yoga, Tai Chi and cognitive behavioural therapy.

cell.label: Take a targeted history to assess characteristics and manifestations of fatigue, including onset, duration, pattern, exacerbating and palliative factors, severity, impact on function. Screen for depression using PHQ.
Perform brief physical exam and order initial lab studies (CBC, TSH, ESR, glucose). If clinically indicated, HIV, Lyme titre, and PPD. Any abnormal?
Schedule second visit for comprehensive history and physical exam. Review laboratory results and order initial studies as clinically indicated. Any abnormal?
Consider consultation. Maintain frequent follow-ups. Educate patient on fatigue management.
